note.text:
We usually count in base ten: ten digits, 0 to 9, and each place is worth ten times the place on its right. In base b there are b digits, 0 to b − 1, and each place is worth b times the place on its right. In base 5 the digits are 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4.

From base ten to base b: divide by b again and again, writing the remainders, until the quotient is 0. Then read the remainders from the bottom to the top.
13 in base 2: 13 ÷ 2 = 6 r 1, 6 ÷ 2 = 3 r 0, 3 ÷ 2 = 1 r 1, 1 ÷ 2 = 0 r 1. So 13 = 1101₂.

From base b to base ten: multiply each digit by its place value and add.
1101₂ = 1 × 8 + 1 × 4 + 0 × 2 + 1 × 1 = 13.

From one base to another: go through base ten.

steps: {idiv(n, b ^ 3)} ÷ {b} = {idiv(n, b ^ 4)} remainder {idiv(n, b ^ 3) % b}. The quotient is now {idiv(n, b ^ 4)}, so we stop.
Read the remainders from the bottom to the top: {toBase(n, b)}{sub(b)}.
Check by going back to base ten: {idiv(n, b ^ 3) % b} × {b ^ 3} + {idiv(n, b ^ 2) % b} × {b ^ 2} + {idiv(n, b) % b} × {b} + {n % b} × {one} = {n}.
checks: (idiv(n, b ^ 3) % b) * b ^ 3 + (idiv(n, b ^ 2) % b) * b ^ 2 + (idiv(n, b) % b) * b + n % b == n
str(idiv(n, b ^ 3) % b) + str(idiv(n, b ^ 2) % b) + str(idiv(n, b) % b) + str(n % b) == toBase(n, b)

cards.idea: In base ten each place is worth ten times the place on its right. In base b we use the digits from {0} up to one less than b, and each place is worth b times the place on its right.
example: The places, from the right, are worth {1}, {b}, {b ^ 2}, {b ^ 3}…

cards.idea: To change from base b to base ten, multiply each digit by its place value and add.

check.hint: Under the two digits, write the place values {b} and {1}. Multiply and add.

cards.idea: To change from base ten to base b, divide by b again and again, writing the remainders, until the quotient is {0}. Read the remainders from the bottom up.

check.hint: Divide {n} by {b}, then divide the quotient by {b}. Read the remainders from the bottom up.

misconceptions.explain: Read the remainders from the bottom up: the last remainder is the first digit.

questions.hint: In base {b}, the only digits allowed are {0} to {b - 1}.
questions.prompt: Which of these cannot be a number in base {b}?
solution: In base {b} the only digits are {join(range(0, b - 1), ', ')}.
{answer} contains the digit {bad_digit}, which is not allowed.

questions.hint: Divide {n} by {b} again and again until the quotient is {0}. Write each remainder, then read them from the bottom up.

misconceptions.explain: Read the remainders from the bottom to the top: the last remainder is the first digit.
Keep dividing by {b} until the quotient is 0. Only remainders are digits of the answer.

questions.hint: Under the digits of {s}, write the place values of base {b}, ending with …, {b}, {1}. Multiply each digit by its place value and add.

misconceptions.explain: {s}{sub(b)} is not the base-ten number {s}. Multiply each digit by its place value in base {b} ({b}{sup(2)}, {b}, 1…) and add.

misconceptions.explain: Changing the base changes the digits. Go through base ten: {s}{sub(b1)} = {n}, then convert {n} to base {b2}.
First change {s}{sub(b1)} to base ten ({n}). Do not treat {s} as a base-ten number.
Read the remainders from the bottom to the top.

solution: First change to base ten: {placeSum(s, b1)}

questions.hint: Check each line: quotient × {b} + remainder must give back the number that was divided.
questions.prompt: Enow converted {n} to base {b}. One line has a mistake. Which one?

steps.text: {n} ÷ {b} = {idiv(n, b)} remainder {w == 0 ? (n % b + 1) % b : n % b}
steps.explain: {n} = {idiv(n, b)} × {b} + {n % b}, so the remainder is {n % b}.

steps.text: {idiv(n, b)} ÷ {b} = {idiv(n, b ^ 2)} remainder {w == 1 ? (idiv(n, b) % b + 1) % b : idiv(n, b) % b}
steps.truth: (w == 1 ? (idiv(n, b) % b + 1) % b : idiv(n, b) % b) == idiv(n, b) % b
steps.explain: {idiv(n, b)} = {idiv(n, b ^ 2)} × {b} + {idiv(n, b) % b}, so the remainder is {idiv(n, b) % b}.

steps.truth: (w == 2 ? reverse(toBase(n, b)) : toBase(n, b)) == toBase(n, b)
steps.explain: The remainders must be read from the bottom to the top: {toBase(n, b)}{sub(b)}.
